step1_analysis.description: A single NMOS transistor, likely extracted as a sub-block (e.g., a buffer, amplifier, or single-ended multiplier stage) from the D-band frequency sixtupler described in the paper.

paper_reference.title: A Compact D-Band CMOS Frequency Sixtupler Using a Mode Analysis of the Harmonics

DC_Drain_Current.description: DC drain current of the NMOS transistor under 0.9V gate bias.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the square-law model with typical sky130 parameters.

Voltage_Gain.description: Low frequency voltage gain with a 1 kOhm load.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm = 2 * Id / Vov = 2 * 311u / 0.48 = 1.29 mA/V. Gain = gm * RL = 1.29 V/V = 2.2 dB
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using estimated gm and a 1k test load. The paper's -0.7 dB is for the full sixtupler conversion gain.

Output_Power.description: Output power at the fundamental frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Pout = Vp^2 / (2*RL). For Vp = 0.258V and RL = 1k, Pout = 33 uW = -14.8 dBm
sky130_expected.reasoning: Estimated for the single transistor testbench. The paper's -1.2 dBm is for the full optimized sixtupler.

Operating_Frequency.description: Target operating frequency of the circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: Testbench uses 100 MHz for basic characterization, as 148 GHz exceeds typical sky130 fmax for simple un-matched stages.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 fT is ~40-50 GHz. The full paper uses advanced harmonic extraction to reach D-band.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to characterize the single NMOS transistor, measuring DC operating point, AC voltage gain, and transient output swing/power.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Single NMOS Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u

XM1 N1 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
RL VDD N1 1k
VIN N0 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 0.2 100Meg)

.control
op
let id = -i(VVDD)
let power = id * 1.8
print id power

ac dec 100 1Meg 10Gig
let gain_db = vdb(N1)
meas ac gain_1M find gain_db at=1Meg
meas ac gain_1G find gain_db at=1Gig

tran 10p 50n
meas tran vout_max max v(N1)
meas tran vout_min min v(N1)
let vout_pp = vout_max - vout_min
let vout_p = vout_pp / 2
let pout_w = (vout_p * vout_p) / (2 * 1000)
let pout_dbm = 10 * log10(pout_w * 1000)
print vout_pp pout_dbm
four 100Meg v(N1)
quit
.endc
